Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.

revision_notes: Internet Society's Pulse country report (ITU/GSMA-sourced) gives Mauritania 4G population coverage of 74%, well above the 35% (2021) originally cited, placing it in the 50-74% band rather than 25-49%. Cross-validated by an exact match on Pulse's cybersecurity index score (39.33) against an independently verified ITU source, increasing confidence in its other figures. Revised code to 3.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The variable requires unique mobile subscriber penetration, but the cited ITU figure (113 subscriptions/100 population) and newer GSMA-based connections data (117-119% of population, DataReportal 2025-26) both measure SIM/connections, which materially overstate unique subscribers due to multi-SIM ownership. No country-specific GSMA unique-subscriber percentage could be located. Flagged for human review rather than confirming or guessing a replacement code.

Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
Comments: No local hyperscale; distant regions (e.g. GCP Johannesburg). [AfriBit](https://www.afribit.co.za/2025/03/27/google-expands-in-africa-how-gcps-new-cloud-region-competes-with-aws/)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. No hyperscale cloud region (AWS, Azure, GCP) exists in Mauritania; the nearest is AWS's Cape Town region, in a different sub-region with high latency. A low-quality aggregator site (stateglobe.com) claims '3 AWS data centres' in Mauritania, but this is unsubstantiated and contradicted by AWS's own infrastructure map — disregarded. Original source (AfriBit, about Johannesburg) was tangential; replaced with primary documentation.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
Comments: Law 2017-020 enacted, DPA regulation 2022, members sworn in (enacted + DPA established). [JD Supra](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/recent-developments-in-african-data-9981570/)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and better sourced. Law No. 2017-020 (22 July 2017) established the data-protection framework; the Autorité de Protection des Données (APD) was formally constituted when its nine members were sworn in in February 2022 and now operates under a 2023-2026 strategic plan. This matches 'legislation enacted with DPA established' (code 4). Original single JDSupra source (a general Africa round-up) replaced with the APD's own site and an independent legal tracker.

Definition: The presence and tier quality of commercial/colocation data center facilities operating in the country. Commercial data centers provide the physical infrastructure for hosting cloud services, content delivery, and enterprise applications domestically.
Comments: Tier III data center built in Nouakchott (small-scale Tier I-III). [EEAS](https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/mauritania/construction-datacenter-nouakchott-mauritania_en)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The National Data Centre in Nouakchott, financed by a EUR15m EIB loan and inaugurated in May 2025, is certified Tier III by the Uptime Institute — confirmed by the EU delegation, the EIB and the US International Trade Administration's commercial guide. This is a Tier III facility, not merely 'small-scale Tier I-II' as originally coded. Revised to 3 ('at least one Tier III facility').

Comments: National Digital Agenda plans national government cloud (basic operational/planned). [Digital Watch](https://dig.watch/resource/mauritanias-national-digital-transformation-agenda-2022-2025)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Ecofin Agency reports Mauritania officially launched its national government cloud platform on 29 June 2026, built on the Tier III National Data Centre in Nouakchott, providing shared computing/storage for government agencies (migration timeline not yet announced). This is more advanced than 'basic government data centre operational' as originally coded — it matches 'national data centre operational with cloud strategy adopted' (code 4), not yet code 5 since active migration has not begun. The launch itself rests on one specialist Africa tech-business outlet, but the underlying Tier III facility is independently corroborated.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Sources materially disagree: the original World Bank appraisal-document comment claims 44% renewable generation (hydro 27%, wind 13%, solar 4%), while countryeconomy.com (IRENA/EIA-derived) gives 22.8% for 2024, and statbase.org's absolute renewable-generation figure (0.263 TWh in 2024) implies a still lower share against total generation of roughly 2.07 TWh. Could not resolve within available time; flagged for human review rather than confirming 25-49% or reverting to a lower band. Recommend checking IRENA's Mauritania country profile directly and distinguishing domestic generation from imported Manantali/OMVS hydropower, which may explain the discrepancy.
